sheet-77.description: Sheet 77 of the 1909 New Jersey coast volume shows the whole settlement of Corson's Inlet, the place renamed Strathmere a few years later, at the north end of the barrier island south of Ocean City. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, so the island runs up the page: the Atlantic Ocean beach is along the right edge and the inlet channel, lettered Corson's Inlet, along the left. Landis Avenue runs the length of the sheet beside the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad right of way, and a second line, the Atlantic City Railroad (Reading), comes in over a trestle across the inlet and curves north alongside it to the railroad depot near Division Avenue. Cross streets from Trenton Avenue at the bottom to Chester Avenue at the top run from the bay to the ocean; Holyday Avenue and Inlet Avenue are short streets on the bay and ocean sides. Almost all of the platted blocks are empty, divided into 25 ft lots and numbered. The few buildings stand along the inlet shore and near the depot: the West Jersey Cottage, the Welen Hotel with its pier, boat houses on piles (Geo. F. Erb, John Stevens, Johnson's, Frank Corson), a few dwellings by the ocean, and a gasoline pumping engine with a 20,000 gallon elevated water tank beside the railroad. The blocks north of Lovell Avenue are drawn deeper than those to the south and their streets are not quite parallel.
notes: Corson's Inlet is today Strathmere, Upper Township.
Landis Avenue is modern Commonwealth Drive; the modern Landis Avenue to the west near the south end follows the old railroad.
Trenton, Reading and Lovell Avenues are modern Prescott Road, Putnam Avenue and Randolph Avenue.

Windmere, Wissahickon, Woodford, Curran, Division and Chester Avenues do not survive on their drawn lines; the area north of Randolph Avenue was replatted with streets from Sherman Avenue to Willard Road.
Holyday Avenue lies on the line of the north part of modern Bayview Drive.
The drawn north arrow points about 10 degrees anticlockwise of true north (magnetic).

Single sheet 77 (N.J. coast map vol. 4), Corson's Inlet, now Strathmere (Upper Township), 100 ft to an inch, north to upper left (true north about -35 deg; the drawn arrow is about 10 deg further anticlockwise, magnetic). Landis Av = modern Commonwealth Drive; Trenton, Reading, Lovell Avs = modern Prescott Road, Putnam Avenue, Randolph Avenue (match within 1-2 m). North of Lovell the 1909 plat differs from the modern grid: Windmere, Wissahickon, Woodford, Curran, Division and Chester Avs are spaced 280-320 ft and fan out, while modern Sherman to Willard are evenly spaced about 250 ft, so none was used as control. Holyday Av matches the north part of modern Bayview Drive (checked on an overlay, within about 4 m). Placed by a helmert on three junctions along one street.
